title: Cache invalidation moved before the DB write, reopening a stale-read window
diff: +    # Invalidate first so we never hold the cache lookup while a DB
+    # write is in flight -- keeps the write transaction short under
+    """Account deletion path: irreversible, so the DB row is gone
+    before the cache entry is dropped, never the other way around."""
+- update_profile now invalidates the profile cache before writing the
+  DB row instead of after, to keep the write transaction short.

ground_truth.explanation: Moving cache.delete() before the DB write reopens the classic cache-invalidation race: between the delete and the DB commit, a concurrent reader can miss the now-empty cache, read the still-pre-write value from the DB, and repopulate the cache with that stale value -- which then serves every subsequent reader for the rest of the cache entry's TTL, not just the one racing request. The comment justifies the reordering as shortening the write transaction, but the original order (write DB, then invalidate) already had that property: the delete is a single fast cache operation either way, and only the after-write ordering guarantees a reader who misses the cache always sees the new value -- the new delete_profile function, added in this same diff, keeps that correct write-then-invalidate order and even says why in its docstring, making update_profile's reordering read as an inconsistency rather than a deliberate, uniform policy change. All eight tests assert on individual calls in isolation and never race a reader against the update, so none of them catch this.\n\nOffline validation (execution_validated): a standalone reproduction with a barrier-synchronized writer and reader against a pre-populated cache entry, 300 trials each ordering. Invalidate-before-write left a stale value permanently cached after the update completed in 300/300 trials (100%); write-before-invalidate did so in 0/300.
ground_truth.validation_note: Standalone threading simulation, barrier-synchronized writer + reader against a pre-populated cache entry, 300 trials per ordering. Invalidate-then-write: stale value persists in cache after the update in 300/300 trials (100%). Write-then-invalidate: 0/300. Script and raw output preserved as private provenance, not in this repository.
